facts.statement: Bambiraptor lived about 72 million years ago in Montana during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Bambiraptor is a genus of bird-like dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous (about 72 million years ago) of Montana.

facts.statement: A 14-year-old named Wes Linster discovered the Bambiraptor skeleton in 1995 near Glacier National Park in Montana.
facts.quote: The Bambiraptor skeleton was discovered in 1995 by 14-year-old fossil hunter Wes Linster, who was looking for dinosaur bones with his parents near Glacier National Park in Montana, United States.

facts.statement: Bambiraptor feinbergi was named and described in 2000 by David Burnham, Kraig Derstler, Phil Currie, Robert Bakker, Zhou Zhonge, and John Ostrom.
facts.quote: In 2000 it was named and described by David Burnham, Kraig Derstler, Phil Currie, Robert Bakker, Zhou Zhonge and John Ostrom as a new genus: Bambiraptor feinbergi.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil is less than 1 meter long and appears to be a juvenile individual.
facts.quote: The holotype fossil is less than 1 m long, although this specimen appears to be a juvenile, and it is possible that Bambiraptor is a juvenile Saurornitholestes.

facts.statement: The species name feinbergi honors the Feinberg family, who acquired the specimen, and references the Disney character Bambi.
facts.quote: Because of its small size, it was named Bambiraptor feinbergi, after the popular Disney movie character (the name literally translates to "Bambi thief") and the surname of the wealthy family who bought and lent the specimen to the new Graves Museum of Natural History in Florida.

facts.statement: The excavation of the holotype skeleton yielded approximately 95 percent completeness.
facts.quote: The bones that Linster discovered on that hilltop led to the excavation of a skeleton that was approximately 95 percent complete.

facts.statement: The juvenile specimen perhaps weighed only two kilograms.
facts.quote: It perhaps weighed only two kilograms (4.4 lb).

facts.statement: Its long hindlimbs suggest it was capable of fast running.
facts.quote: It had long hindlimbs, indicating it could have been a fast runner.

facts.statement: The dinosaur possessed very long arms and a well-developed wishbone.
facts.quote: It also had very long arms and a well-developed wishbone.

facts.statement: Research suggests Bambiraptor may have had opposable first and third fingers allowing it to place food in its mouth.
facts.quote: Research done by Phil Senter of the Lamar State College in Orange, Texas has indicated that Bambiraptor may have had mutually opposable first and third fingers and a forelimb maneuverability that would allow the hand to reach its mouth.

facts.statement: Bambiraptor had a brain size comparable to the lower range of modern birds.
facts.quote: Bambiraptor had a brain size in the lower range of modern birds.

facts.statement: David A. Burnham hypothesized that Bambiraptor may have been arboreal based on its enlarged cerebellum.
facts.quote: Because of its enlarged cerebellum, which may indicate higher agility and higher intelligence than other dromaeosaurs, David A. Burnham has hypothesized that Bambiraptor feinbergi may have been arboreal.

facts.statement: The holotype had a brain volume of 14 cm³, the largest for its size of any dinosaur discovered, though this may be due to its juvenile age.
facts.quote: The Bambiraptor holotype had with 14 cm3 the largest brain for its size of any dinosaur yet discovered, although the brain size may be due to its age, because juvenile animals tend to have larger brain-to-body ratios compared to adults.

facts.statement: Bambiraptor is classified within the family Dromaeosauridae, though its exact position within the family remains uncertain.
facts.quote: Bambiraptor was assigned to the Dromaeosauridae in 2000, though its position within the family remains uncertain, since subsequent cladistic analyses show different results.

facts.statement: Bambiraptor belongs to the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: Bambiraptor is placed in the subfamily Saurornitholestinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Saurornitholestinae

facts.statement: It is debated whether Bambiraptor is a distinct genus or merely a juvenile Saurornitholestes.
facts.quote: it is possible that Bambiraptor is a juvenile Saurornitholestes.

facts.statement: Some researchers suspect the holotype specimen is a chimera because it contains elements from three different similarly sized lower legs.
facts.quote: It is even suspected that the type specimen is a chimera, based on the fact that "there are elements of three different similarly sized lower legs included in the holotype."

facts.statement: Bambiraptor stood approximately 0.3 meters tall, 0.7 meters long, and weighed only 2 kilograms.
facts.quote: Cuando estaba vivo Bambiraptor habría medido alrededor, de 0,3 metros de alto y 0,7 de largo pesando solo 2 kilogramos

facts.statement: Bambiraptor had a large brain similar to that of modern birds.
facts.quote: Bambiraptor tenía un cerebro de gran tamaño, similar al de las aves modernas.

facts.statement: Bambiraptor possessed the largest brain-to-body size ratio of any discovered dinosaur.
facts.quote: Bambiraptor tenía el cerebro más grande para su tamaño de cualquier dinosaurio descubierto

facts.statement: Research suggests Bambiraptor may have possessed opposable front claws.
facts.quote: La investigación hecha en Universidad Estatal de Lamar de Orange, Tejas ha indicado que Bambiraptor puede haber tenido las garras delanteras oponibles

facts.statement: Bambiraptor likely had feathers due to its phylogenetic position within the group Paraves.
facts.quote: Bambiraptor probablemente tenía plumas debido a su posición filogenética.

facts.statement: The holotype of Bambiraptor was discovered in 1993.
facts.quote: El holotipo fue descubierto en 1993

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is currently housed in the American Museum of Natural History in New York.
facts.quote: El espécimen se guarda actualmente en Museo Americano de Historia Natural en Nueva York.

facts.statement: The Bambiraptor skeleton was discovered in 1993 by 14-year-old fossil hunter Wes Linster.
facts.quote: El esqueleto de Bambiraptor fue descubierto en 1993 por el cazador de fósiles Wes Linster, de 14 años de edad

facts.statement: The excavation led to the discovery of a skeleton that was 95 percent complete.
facts.quote: Los huesos que Linster descubrió en esa colina llevaron a la excavación de un esqueleto que estaba completo en un 95 por ciento.

facts.statement: Bambiraptor feinbergi was named and described as a separate species in 2000 by David Burnham, Kraig Derstler, Phil Currie, Robert Bakker, Zhou Zhonge, and John Ostrom.
facts.quote: En 2000 fue nombrado y descrito por David Burnham, Kraig Derstler, Phil Currie, Robert Bakker, Zhou Zhonge y John Ostrom como especie separada: Bambiraptor feinbergi

facts.statement: The genus name derives from 'Bambi,' referencing the specimen's young age, and 'raptor,' from the Latin for 'plunderer'.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva de Bambi , en referencia a la corta edad de la muestra, y raptor, del latín rapaz

facts.statement: The species name honors Michael and Ann Feinberg, who acquired the specimen from a fossil dealer and donated it to science.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, se deriva de Michael y Ann Feinberg que adquirieron la muestra de un distribuidor fósiles, y lo cedieron a la ciencia.

facts.statement: Bambiraptor lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: David A. Burnham hypothesized that Bambiraptor may have been arboreal.
facts.quote: David A. Burnham ha presumido que Bambiraptor feinbergi puede haber sido arbóreo.

facts.statement: An alternative hypothesis suggests the large brain evolved to hunt agile prey such as lizards and mammals.
facts.quote: Burnham también ofrece una hipótesis alternativa que un cerebro más grande se podría seleccionar como resultado de cazar presas más ágiles tales como lagartos y mamíferos.

facts.statement: Opposable claws would have allowed the animal to grasp food with its forelimbs and carry it to its mouth, similar to some modern small mammals.
facts.quote: Esto habría dado al animal la capacidad de "tomar" el alimento en sus miembros delanteros y llevarlo a su boca, de una manera similar a algunos pequeños mamíferos modernos.

facts.statement: While described as a new taxon within Dromaeosauridae, some believe it should be synonymized with Saurornitholestes.
facts.quote: Fue descrito como un nuevo taxón dentro de Dromaeosauridae, aunque algunos creen que debe ser sinonimizado con Saurornitholestes.

facts.statement: Published phylogenetic analyses have placed Bambiraptor far from Saurornitholestes.
facts.quote: Bambiraptor se ha colocado en los análisis cladísticos lejos de Saurornitholestes en análisis filogenéticos publicados.
